# `accountant-copy` commands

## `accountant-copy cancel`

Remove the accountant's copy restrictions without importing, as the anchor's Remove Restrictions does: these books take changes on or before the dividing date again, and the copy's change file can no longer be imported. Needs a reason. A person's step.

A dry run previews the proposed result without saving it. Any proposed record IDs or posted status in that preview describe the prospective save, not an existing saved record.

| Contract | Value |
|---|---|
| Scope | company |
| Kind | write |
| Required role | admin |
| Capability | company |
| Feature | — |
| HTTP | `POST /companies/{company_id}/commands/accountant-copy.cancel` |
| External binary body | none |

### CLI

`bookflow accountant-copy cancel --reason "Accountant sent a list of entries instead" --company "Demo Plumbing Co" --json`

## `accountant-copy changes`

In an accountant's copy: write the change file to send back, in the company folder's exports/. It holds every adjusting entry and reclassification made in the copy (each as it stands now; voided ones are left out), notes, review marks and reviewed-through marks, signed so the owner's books can tell it came unaltered from this copy. Run it again after more work; the owner imports one file, which closes the copy.

A dry run previews the proposed result without saving it. Any proposed record IDs or posted status in that preview describe the prospective save, not an existing saved record.

## `accountant-copy export`

Make an accountant's copy, as the anchor does: a verified backup archive of the company (open it on the accountant's machine with `company restore --as-copy`) whose books know the dividing date `through`, with a small manifest beside it, in the company folder's exports/. Bookflow sends it nowhere; hand it over yourself. While the copy is out these books refuse every change dated on or before the dividing date, and account edits and list merges, until `accountant-copy import` takes the accountant's changes back or a person runs `accountant-copy cancel`. The copy takes only adjusting entries, reclassifications, review marks and notes dated on or before the dividing date. The copy is for one designated external accountant (`accountant`; default the one designated, and one must be): every change it sends back is posted as them. The dividing date must be after the closing date. No backup ever carries the key that verifies the copy's change file. An agent may prepare this hand-off.

A dry run previews the proposed result without saving it. Any proposed record IDs or posted status in that preview describe the prospective save, not an existing saved record.

| Contract | Value |
|---|---|
| Scope | company |
| Kind | write |
| Required role | admin |
| Capability | company |
| Feature | — |
| HTTP | `POST /companies/{company_id}/commands/accountant-copy.export` |
| External binary body | none |

### CLI

`bookflow accountant-copy export 2026-09-30 --reason "Q3 review by our accountant" --company "Demo Plumbing Co" --json`

### MCP

The same example as complete `bookflow_run` arguments:

```json

```

### Input

|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `accountant` | `--accountant` | string \| null | no | yes | null | Username or user id of the designated external accountant the copy is for; default the one designated. Every change the copy sends back is posted as them. |
| `through` | `THROUGH` | string | yes | no | — | Dividing date, YYYY-MM-DD: the accountant works on or before it; these books then refuse changes dated on or before it until the copy comes back or is cancelled.; minimum length 10; maximum length 10 |

## `accountant-copy import`

Take an accountant's changes back from their change file, as the anchor's Import Accountant's Changes: every new change, or only the keys in `changes`. Each is posted as the external accountant the copy was made for (never as a name the file gives), under its own audit event naming the copy and the accountant's reason; each change is taken at most once. The copy comes back and is closed: these books take changes on or before the dividing date again, changes left out are declined, and the file (or any other for that copy) is refused from then on. A person's step: an agent may preview, never import.

A dry run previews the proposed result without saving it. Any proposed record IDs or posted status in that preview describe the prospective save, not an existing saved record.

| Contract | Value |
|---|---|
| Scope | company |
| Kind | write |
| Required role | admin |
| Capability | company |
| Feature | — |
| HTTP | `POST /companies/{company_id}/commands/accountant-copy.import` |
| External binary body | none |

### CLI

`bookflow accountant-copy import "/home/owner/Downloads/Demo Plumbing Co accountant changes 2026-10-14-091500.json" --reason "Q3 adjustments" --company "Demo Plumbing Co" --json`

### MCP

The same example as complete `bookflow_run` arguments:

```json
{"command": "accountant-copy import", "input": {"file": "/home/owner/Downloads/Demo Plumbing Co accountant changes 2026-10-14-091500.json"}, "company": "Company ID or name", "dry_run": true, "reason": "Preview the requested change"}
```

### Input

| JSON field | CLI input | Type | Required | Nullable | Default | Description and constraints |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `file` | `FILE` | string | yes | no | — | Full path of the accountant's change file on the machine running Bookflow.; minimum length 1; maximum length 4096 |
| `changes` | `--changes` | array[string] \| null | no | yes | null | Keys of the changes to take (from `accountant-copy preview`); default every new change. |
| `close_copy` | `--close-copy` | boolean | no | no | false | Close the copy even though this import takes none of its changes (all are declined). |

### Command and context options

|---|---|
| `--json` | Print one JSON object. |

| `--directive TEXT` | Standing-instruction code or id cited by the write. |
| `--company TEXT` | Company id, `Organization/Company`, or display name. |

### HTTP

Route: `POST /companies/{company_id}/commands/accountant-copy.import`

Send the input object as JSON. Authentication may instead come from a browser session cookie.

| Header | Requirement | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `Authorization` | required for bearer clients | `Bearer <secret>` |
| `X-Bookflow-Client-Name` | optional | Stable caller name recorded in audit |
| `X-Bookflow-Client-Version` | optional | Caller version recorded in audit |
| `X-Bookflow-Context-Encoding` | optional | percent-utf8: encode all reason, source-ref, directive, idempotency-key, client-name and client-version header values as UTF-8 percent encoding |
| `X-Bookflow-Company` | optional | If sent, must equal the company ULID in the route |
| `X-Bookflow-Reason` | conditional | Short reason; an agent or system write needs this or an active directive |
| `X-Bookflow-Source-Ref` | optional | Identifier of the source that triggered the write |
| `X-Bookflow-Directive` | conditional | Active directive code or id; alternative to reason for an agent or system write |

### Output

| JSON field | Type | Required | Nullable | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `copy_id` | string | yes | no | — | — |
| `company_id` | string | yes | no | — | — |
| `dividing_date` | string | yes | no | — | — |
| `accountant_name` | string \| null | yes | yes | — | The external accountant the copy was made for, from these books. |
| `named_in_file_as` | string \| null | no | yes | null | A different accountant name the file gives: a label only. |
| `created_at` | string | yes | no | — | — |
| `changes` | array[object] | yes | no | — | — |
| `changes[].key` | string | yes | no | — | Stable key of the change in its file. |
| `changes[].kind` | literal["journal", "reclassification", "note", "review_mark", "reviewed_through"] | yes | no | — | — |
| `changes[].date` | string \| null | yes | yes | — | Accounting date (an entry) or reviewed-through date; null for a note. |
| `changes[].summary` | string | yes | no | — | — |
| `changes[].reason` | string \| null | yes | yes | — | The accountant's reason, as their copy recorded it. |
| `changes[].by_name` | string \| null | yes | yes | — | The external accountant the copy was made for, from these books: every change is posted as them. |
| `changes[].named_in_file_as` | string \| null | no | yes | null | A different name the file gives for whoever entered it: a label only, never who the change is posted as. |
| `changes[].lines` | array[object] | no | no | [] | — |
| `changes[].lines[].account_id` | string | yes | no | — | — |
| `changes[].lines[].account_name` | string \| null | yes | yes | — | — |
| `changes[].lines[].side` | literal["debit", "credit"] | yes | no | — | — |
| `changes[].lines[].amount` | string | yes | no | — | — |
| `changes[].lines[].description` | string \| null | no | yes | null | — |
| `changes[].state` | literal["new", "imported", "refused"] | yes | no | — | new: can be taken; imported: already taken (by result_id); refused: cannot be taken, see problem. |
| `changes[].problem` | string \| null | no | yes | null | — |
| `changes[].result_id` | string \| null | no | yes | null | — |
| `counts` | object[string, integer] | yes | no | — | Changes by state. |
| `dry_run` | boolean | no | no | false | — |
| `warnings` | array[string] | no | no | [] | — |
| `imported` | array[string] | yes | no | — | Keys of the changes taken by this import. |
| `declined` | integer | no | no | 0 | Changes in the file this import leaves out; the copy closes, so they are declined for good. |
| `status` | string | yes | no | — | The copy's status after the import. |

```json
  "counts": {},

  "dry_run": false,
  "imported": [],
  "named_in_file_as": null,
  "status": "value",
  "warnings": []
}
```

## `accountant-copy preview`

Verify an accountant's change file against these books and list each change: new (can be taken), imported (already taken) or refused (and why). A file changed after the copy wrote it, or from another company's or another copy's books, is refused whole. Nothing is changed.

| Contract | Value |
|---|---|
| Scope | company |
| Kind | read |
| Required role | admin |
| Capability | company |
| Feature | — |
| HTTP | `POST /companies/{company_id}/commands/accountant-copy.preview` |
| External binary body | none |

### CLI

`bookflow accountant-copy preview "/home/owner/Downloads/Demo Plumbing Co accountant changes 2026-10-14-091500.json" --company "Demo Plumbing Co" --json`

### MCP

The same example as complete `bookflow_run` arguments:

```json
{"command": "accountant-copy preview", "input": {"file": "/home/owner/Downloads/Demo Plumbing Co accountant changes 2026-10-14-091500.json"}, "company": "Company ID or name"}
```

| JSON field | CLI input | Type | Required | Nullable | Default | Description and constraints |

| `file` | `FILE` | string | yes | no | — | Full path of the accountant's change file on the machine running Bookflow.; minimum length 1; maximum length 4096 |

## `accountant-copy status`

Whether an accountant's copy is out and its dividing date (these books refuse changes on or before it), or, in an accountant's copy, the date it is restricted to; with earlier copies.

| Contract | Value |
|---|---|
| Scope | company |
| Kind | read |
| Required role | member |
| Capability | company |
| Feature | — |
| HTTP | `POST /companies/{company_id}/commands/accountant-copy.status` |
| External binary body | none |

### CLI

`bookflow accountant-copy status --company "Demo Plumbing Co" --json`

### MCP

The same example as complete `bookflow_run` arguments:

```json
{"command": "accountant-copy status", "input": {}, "company": "Company ID or name"}
```

| — | — | — | — | — | — | This command has no input fields. |

| Option | Meaning |

| `--company TEXT` | Company id, `Organization/Company`, or display name. |

Send the input object as JSON. Authentication may instead come from a browser session cookie.
